blocks.rationale: No installed skill contains a coupled constant block eligible for lift. This joint free-repair package adds source-grounded terminal helpers for all three trigger parents: one computes airline totals from current measurements and current fee schedules, and one applies Illinois's current-source wildcard personal-property exemption while preserving EC/EV native output forms.

skill.intent: Compute the exact integer ticket-plus-fees total from the current passenger's item measurements and the checked-bag, cabin, route, oversize, and overweight schedules stated in the current source.

outputs.description: The exact integer ticket price plus all applicable current checked-bag base fees and higher-of-oversize-or-overweight surcharges.
outputs.name: answer

origin.quote: The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.

source_obligations.statement: Apply the current carry-on dimensional allowance once before assigning checked-bag positions.

origin.quote: For First / Business, weight is 70 lbs / 32 kgs for complimentary bags and 50 lbs / 23 kgs for excess charged bags

source_obligations.statement: Select the checked-position, oversize, overweight, and cabin weight entries applicable to the current itinerary.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: For each checked bag, add its position-based fee and only the higher applicable size or weight surcharge, then add the ticket price.

source_provenance.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.
We calculate the size limits of your bag by adding the total outside dimensions of each bag, length + width + height.
The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

origin.quote: The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

source_obligations.statement: For each current asset, check that it is personal rather than business property and therefore falls within Illinois's any-other-property exemption.

origin.quote: The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $4,000 in value, in any other property;

source_obligations.statement: Limit each independently evaluated asset claim to the available exemption interests of the current debtor or joint debtors.

source_provenance.quote:
735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $4,000 in value, in any other property;
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.
